subject: Geopolitics
title: AUKUS and the Indo-Pacific
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: AUKUS and the Indo-Pacific.

hook.text: Australia abandoned a $90 billion French submarine deal for US nuclear subs. France was not informed in advance.

buildup.text: AUKUS — Australia, UK, US — is a defense pact focused on giving Australia nuclear submarine capability.

discovery.text: The real goal is containing China in the Indo-Pacific. Nuclear subs can patrol vast ocean distances for months.

twist.text: AUKUS angered France and divided allies. The deal showed that Indo-Pacific security now trumps European feelings.

climax.text: AUKUS signals a tectonic shift: the center of gravity in Western strategy is moving from the Atlantic to the Pacific.

punchline.text: New threats demand new alliances, even at old friends' expense.

quiz.question: What is the primary strategic goal of AUKUS?
options: Securing trade routes through the Atlantic
Containing China in the Indo-Pacific region
Replacing NATO as the main Western alliance
